talking_points.headline: US-bank agent controls emphasise containment and continuity
talking_points.context_html: The report says some US banks are tightening agent permissions, preserving activity records, reviewing kill switches and preparing backup processes, while reporting no bank incidents of this kind to date. A practical change criterion is whether a shutdown can preserve evidence and hand work to a tested fallback for functions such as loan processing or financial-crime review. The detail comes largely from unnamed sources and does not establish how widely or effectively the controls are in use.

talking_points.headline: ECB sets conditions for DLT collateral eligibility
talking_points.context_html: The ECB approved eligibility for certain DLT-issued assets subject to standard collateral criteria and added operational requirements, with details expected in spring 2027 and implementation planned for June 2027. For banking operations, a key delivery dependency is demonstrating a compliant route through an eligible CSD and TARGET2-Securities, alongside legal certainty and safe handling of critical functions. This is a European collateral-framework development; the article does not indicate direct APAC implementation requirements.

talking_points.headline: Standard Chartered describes a targeted India wealth strategy
talking_points.context_html: Standard Chartered India’s CEO said the bank is deepening relationships with target retail clients and continuing to invest in wealth offerings. For wealth delivery, the stated segmentation implies a capacity trade-off between serving a fuller range of needs for selected clients and maintaining relationships outside that target; the interview gives no operational detail or evidence of outcomes. These are management statements about India, not evidence of a region-wide change.

AI & Technology.title: Some US banks tighten AI-agent controls on concern about models escaping safeguards
AI & Technology.summary: The Economic Times reports, citing banking and industry sources, that several US banks are tightening controls on internal AI agents, including restricting system access and credentials, isolating test environments, recording agent actions, reviewing kill switches and preparing backup processes. Sources describe these measures as responses to concerns about models bypassing safeguards; the report says no banks had yet been affected by such incidents. For banking operations, the measures highlight dependencies between agent permissions, auditability and continuity when an agent is stopped; the article is based substantially on unnamed sources and does not establish the prevalence or effectiveness of the controls.

Competitor Intelligence.title: SBI Chief AI Officer: Bank Offers Up to Rs 1.6 Crore Salary for Top AI Role
Competitor Intelligence.summary: The Open Press reports that State Bank of India is recruiting a chief AI officer to oversee its enterprise AI platform and agentic AI work, alongside five other senior technology appointments covering governance, compliance, data engineering, operations and architecture. SBI says the chief AI officer’s annual compensation is negotiable up to Rs 1.6 crore, not guaranteed. The hiring plan highlights the range of specialist capabilities a bank may assemble for AI delivery, but the article does not establish that SBI has filled the roles or deployed new capabilities.

Competitor Intelligence.title: DBS new retail multi-asset fund raises $200m in two weeks
Competitor Intelligence.summary: Asian Banking & Finance reports that DBS launched a retail multi-asset fund which raised more than S$200 million during its two-week initial offer period, with subscriptions continuing through the bank’s digital app. DBS says the fund is managed by its discretionary portfolio management team and actively allocated and rebalanced to its CIO’s house view. The launch illustrates a digital distribution and managed-investment proposition for retail clients; the reported fundraising and historical strategy returns do not establish future performance or ongoing client demand.

Competitor Intelligence.title: Every Indian today is a global Indian: PD Singh of Standard Chartered Bank
Competitor Intelligence.summary: Standard Chartered India CEO PD Singh described the bank’s focus on deeper relationships with target retail customers, including continued investment in wealth management, Signature Funds in GIFT City and SC Autograph. He also cited cross-border and corporate activity as opportunities for the franchise. The remarks provide competitor context on positioning and client segmentation; they do not specify implementation plans, operating results for the named offerings, or APAC-wide service changes.

Private Banking & Wealth.title: Bank Of Singapore Adds To ASEAN Private Banking Team - Wealth Briefing Asia
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: Bank of Singapore appointed Veronica Darwin as ASEAN cluster head for Indonesia and Minda Melinda as a relationship manager, both based in Singapore, to strengthen its HNW and UHNW capabilities. The appointments indicate competitor investment in ASEAN private-banking coverage; the report gives no detail on service or operating-model changes.

Regulatory & Markets.title: UBS Overweight On Indian Banks; HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank Remain Top Picks
Regulatory & Markets.summary: UBS remains overweight on Indian banks and identifies HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank and Axis Bank as preferred picks, citing loan growth and earnings fundamentals while noting increased early delinquencies in gold loans relative to June. The analysis offers a market and credit-risk perspective relevant to regional competitor intelligence; it is a brokerage assessment, not evidence of future performance.

Regulatory & Markets.title: ECB expands acceptance of DLT-based assets as eligible Eurosystem collateral
Regulatory & Markets.summary: On 23 November 2026, the ECB approved eligibility as Eurosystem collateral for certain marketable assets issued on DLT platforms licensed under the EU DLT Pilot Regime, provided standard criteria and operational requirements are met. The ECB expects to communicate detailed requirements in spring 2027 and plans implementation for June 2027. For banking change execution, this makes legal certainty, settlement-system links and operational safety concrete delivery dependencies; the decision concerns eligible collateral in the Eurosystem, not broad acceptance of all on-chain assets.
